rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade includes buying and selling, but sale is named because its certain, immediate profit distracts more than the uncertain future gain of purchase.
rows.anchor: أن التجارة جنس يدخل تحت أنواع الشراء والبيع إلا أنه / سبحانه خص البيع بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sale exchanges goods for cash, while purchase reverses that exchange; desire for acquiring cash is stronger.
rows.anchor: أن البيع يقتضي تبديل العرض بالنقد ، والشراء بالعكس

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says trade is importing goods from another place, while sale is what a person sells with his own hands.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : التجارة لأهل الجلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Men are specified because al-Rāzī says women are not among those engaged in commerce or congregational gatherings.
rows.anchor: لأن النساء لسن من أهل التجارات أو الجماعات

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One view takes remembrance of God to mean praising Him and making supplications.
rows.anchor: فقال قوم : المراد الثناء على الله تعالى والدعوات

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view takes remembrance of God to mean the prayers themselves.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : المراد الصلوات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains establishing prayer as performing it at its appointed times.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما المراد بإقام الصلاة إقامتها لمواقيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī allows “righteousness is not…” to explain remembrance: they remember God before prayer and during it.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون قوله : { ليس البر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer means fulfilling its due rights according to its conditions, as al-Rāzī explained under al-Baqara 2:3.
rows.anchor: إقام الصلاة هو القيام بحقها على شروطها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives iqāma from aqāma: the wāw becomes alif, one adjacent alif is deleted, and tāʾ compensates for the deletion.
rows.anchor: ما قاله الزجاج ، يقال أقمت الصلاة إقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive construction compensates for the deleted tāʾ; al-Rāzī says grammarians unanimously accept the analysis.
rows.anchor: وقامت الإضافة ههنا في التعويض مقام الهاء المحذوفة ، قال وهذا إجماع من النحويين

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One view restricts prayer here to obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: اختلفوا في الصلاة فمنهم من قال هي الفرائض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view includes voluntary prayer, as in the cited report from Ibn ʿAbbās about the ḍuḥā prayer.
rows.anchor: على ما حكيناه في صلاة الضحى عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers obligatory prayer because it is more precise as a definition and matches the established legal term.
rows.anchor: والأول أقرب لأنه إلى التعريف أقرب وكذلك القول في الزكاة أن المراد المفروض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat means the obligatory due, the established legal meaning of the term; its connection to giving points to a property payment.
rows.anchor: المراد المفروض لأنه المعروف في الشرع المسمى بذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives zakat the broader sense of obeying God and sincerity, also applying that sense in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما المراد من الزكاة طاعة الله تعالى والإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the broad sense: zakat is connected to giving and therefore denotes what is paid from property.
rows.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لما تقدم ولأنه تعالى علق الزكاة بالإيتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though devoted to remembrance and worship, these men fear Judgment Day because they know they have not worshipped God as He deserves.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الرجال وإن تعبدوا بذكر الله والطاعات فإنهم مع ذلك موصوفون بالوجل والخوف

rows.speaker: القول الأول
rows.claim: The first explanation is that hearts convulse with terror and eyes stare in horror.
rows.anchor: فالقول الأول أن القلوب تضطرب من الهول والفزع وتشخص الأبصار

rows.speaker: القول الثاني
rows.claim: Hearts and eyes change: the previously uncomprehending heart understands and the formerly blind eye sees, moving from doubt to certainty and then direct witnessing.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنها تتغير أحوالها فتفقه القلوب بعد أن كانت مطبوعا عليها لا تفقه

rows.speaker: القول الثالث
rows.claim: Hearts swing between hope of rescue and fear of ruin, while eyes turn anxiously toward where people will be led and where their books will come from.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أن القلوب تتقلب في ذلك اليوم طمعا في النجابة وحذرا من الهلاك

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites reject the third explanation: the saved have no fear and the punished do not hope for pardon; al-Rāzī says he has already refuted their position.
rows.anchor: والمعتزلة لا يرضون بهذا التأويل ، فإنهم قالوا إن أهل الثواب لا خوف عليهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the disbeliever is raised with keen sight, his eyes turn blue and then go blind, and fear drives his heart up to his throat.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك : يحشر الكافر وبصره حديد وتزرق عيناه ثم يعمى

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says punishment changes the hearts’ and eyes’ appearance, like flesh being roasted or burned; he also allows that they turn over Hellfire’s embers.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي المراد بتقلب القلوب والأبصار تغير هيئاتهما بسبب ما ينالها من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra discusses divine unity, prophecy, and resurrection, then ends with traits of devoted believers; it begins with the Creator and His attributes because these should come first.
rows.anchor: ولما كان إثبات الصانع وإثبات صفات جلاله يجب أن يكون مقدما على الكل لا جرم افتتح الله هذه السورة بذلك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives tabāraka from baraka, “blessing”; blessing means abundant and increasing good, as in 14:34.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : تبارك : تفاعل من البركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī explains tabāraka as God’s transcendence above all things in essence, attributes, and actions, citing 42:11.
rows.anchor: والثاني : تزايد عن كل شيء وتعالى عنه في ذاته وصفاته وأفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transcendence in essence may mean that God’s necessary existence and eternity exclude extinction and change, or that His unity excludes resemblance to contingent beings.
rows.anchor: جل بوجوب وجوده وقدمه عن جواز الفناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In attributes, God’s knowledge is beyond human categories of necessary or acquired knowledge and conception or assent; His power needs no matter, duration, model, or acquired benefit.
rows.anchor: جل أن يكون علمه ضروريا أو كسبيا أو تصورا أو تصديقا وفي قدرته أن يحتاج إلى مادة ومدة ومثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In action, existence, its persistence, and its sound ordering come only from God.
rows.anchor: في أفعاله فجل أن يكون الوجود والبقاء وصلاح حال الوجود إلا من قبله

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other linguists derive the word from permanence, linking it to a camel or bird settling and to a pool where water remains; God is everlasting and unchanging.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : أصل الكلمة تدل على البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God creates and preserves benefits and interests, al-Rāzī says He rightly bears the description tabāraka.
rows.anchor: ولما كان سبحانه وتعالى هو الخالق لوجوه المنافع والمصالح والمبقى لها وجب وصفه سبحانه بأنه تبارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the audience did not know that God sent down the Furqān, the relative pronoun is apt because proof of the Qur’an’s miraculousness establishes its divine origin so clearly that it is treated as known.
rows.anchor: فلقوة الدليل وظهوره أجراه سبحانه وتعالى مجرى المعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is called Furqān because it distinguishes truth from falsehood about Muhammad’s prophethood and separates lawful from unlawful.
rows.anchor: وصف بذلك من حيث إنه سبحانه فرق به بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers that Furqān refers to the Qur’an’s piecemeal revelation: “nazzala” signals division, while “anzala” signals sending down as a whole, as 3:3 contrasts the Book with Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: وهذا التأويل أقرب لأنه قال : { نزل الفرقان } ولفظة ( نزل ) تدل على التفريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the blessing description is followed by mention of the Qur’an, it is a source of blessings; as a source of knowledge, wisdom, and understanding, knowledge is the noblest and most beneficial creation.
rows.anchor: دل ذلك على أن القرآن منشأ الخيرات وأعم البركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant mentioned here is Muhammad.
rows.anchor: لا نزاع أن المراد من العبد ههنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads “upon His servants” in the plural, meaning Muhammad and his community, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن الزبير على عباده وهم رسول الله وأمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī takes “a warner to the worlds” as Muhammad, the servant, since warning is literally an agent’s attribute.
rows.anchor: فالمراد ليكون هذا العبد نذيرا للعالمين

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take the Qur’an as the referent, metaphorically calling it a warner as it is called a guide in 17:9; al-Rāzī rejects this as less literal.
rows.anchor: وقول من قال : إنه راجع إلى الفرقان فأضاف الإنذار إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The worlds” includes all creatures and accountable beings, including jinn, humans, and angels; since Muhammad was not sent to angels, he must have been sent to all jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: يتناول جميع المكلفين من الجن والإنس والملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because “the worlds” includes all creatures, Muhammad’s mission extends to all creation through the end of time, establishing him as the final prophet and messenger.
rows.anchor: يتناول جميع المخلوقات فدلت الآية على أنه رسول للخلق

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer that God wills faith and obedience from everyone because He sent Muhammad to warn everyone.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة دلت الآية على أنه سبحانه أراد الإيمان وفعل الطاعات من الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī’s school counters the Muʿtazilite inference with 7:179, which says God created some for Hell.
rows.anchor: وعارضهم أصحابنا بقوله تعالى : { ولقد ذرأنا لجهنم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although warning brings fear, it fits the blessing theme like disciplining a child: greater warning can bring greater return to God and lasting happiness, directing attention to religious rather than worldly benefit.
rows.anchor: كلما كان الإنذار كثيرا كان رجوع الخلق إلى الله أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ownership of the heavens and earth points to His existence: His effects depend on Him, so this attribute properly precedes the others.
rows.anchor: لا طريق إلى إثباته إلا بواسطة احتياج أفعاله إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth depends on God for origination, persistence, essence, and existence, and He disposes of it as He wills.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى احتياج هذه المخلوقات إليه سبحانه بزمان حدوثها وزمان بقائها في ماهيتها وفي وجودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God takes no child: He alone is eternally worshipped, and no one inherits sovereignty from Him; this reinforces the opening and refutes Christians.
rows.anchor: فبين سبحانه أنه هو المعبود أبدا

words: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٌۭ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is divine; recognizing this cuts off fear and hope directed to other beings and refutes dualists and worshippers of stars or idols.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنه هو المنفرد بالإلهية ، وإذا عرف العبد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says “He created everything” includes human acts, since acts are things.
rows.anchor: يتناول جميع الأشياء فيتناول أفعال العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also answers those who deny other gods yet claim to create their own acts, following the denial of partners.
rows.anchor: لما نفى الشريك كأن قائلا قال : ههنا أقوام يعترفون

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that the verse cannot imply God creates human acts because scripture calls the servant a creator and calls God the best of creators.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي الآية لا تدل عليه لوجوه : أحدها

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that because God praises Himself for creation, the verse cannot refer to creating evil.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أنه سبحانه تمدح بذلك فلا يجوز أن يريد به خلق الفساد

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that God’s praise for precise apportionment can refer only to good and wise things, not evil.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أنه سبحانه تمدح بأنه قدره تقديرا ولا يجوز أن يريد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī relays al-Qāḍī’s argument that creation means apportionment, which appears only in bodies, not accidents.
rows.anchor: لأن الخلق عبارة عن التقدير فهو لا يتناول إلا ما يظهر فيه التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that the servant-creator verses are countered by 39:62, “God is creator of everything,” and 35:3, “Is there any creator besides God?”
rows.anchor: فهما معارضان بقوله : { الله خالق كل شىء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may be praised for creating evil insofar as it displays the scope of His power to bring things from nonexistence into existence and extinguish them.
rows.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يقع التمدح به نظرا إلى تقادير القدرة وإلى أن صفة الإيجاد من العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If creation applied only to bodies, the statement “He created everything” would wrongly ascribe creation to things that cannot rationally be said to be created.
rows.anchor: لو كان كذلك لكان قوله { خلق كل * شىء } خطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is not repeated estimation: God originates each thing with measure and order, preparing it for what suits it and its proper purpose.
rows.anchor: إحداثا يراعي فيه التقدير والتسوية ، فقدره تقديرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are formed in balanced shape for religious and worldly duties and interests; every animal and inanimate thing is made in wise proportion for a fitting purpose.
rows.anchor: مثاله أنه خلق الإنسان على هذا الشكل المقدر ( المستوي ) الذي تراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine estimation is knowledge and truthful disclosure, unlike human conjecture; what God knows will not occur cannot occur, or His knowledge would become ignorance and His truthful report a lie. Thus command and will do not always coincide.
rows.anchor: أما في حقه سبحانه فلا معنى له إلا العلم به والإخبار عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If an act is necessary once power and motive are complete, the servant’s act would necessitate God’s act; if not, it is either an uncaused possibility or requires a chain of determinants ending at the Necessary Existent.
rows.anchor: عند حصول القدرة والداعية الخالصة إن وجب الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People seek knowledge and truth but often acquire ignorance and falsehood; explaining each error by an earlier error regresses, while self-caused ignorance is impossible, so all occurs by God’s pervasive decree.
rows.anchor: لكن الإنسان لا يريد إلا العلم والحق فلا يحصل له إلا الجهل والباطل

words: لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ
rows.speaker: الذين كفروا
rows.claim: The Meccans objected that Muhammad claimed prophethood but the Qur’an was not sent all at once, as the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms were.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن هذا هو الشبهة الخامسة لمنكري نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ
rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says there were twenty-two or twenty-three years between the beginning and end of revelation.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن جريج بين أوله وآخره اثنتان أو ثلاث وعشرون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Muhammad could neither read nor write, receiving the Qur’an all at once could have exceeded his ability to retain it and exposed him to mistakes or forgetfulness; the Torah was written for Moses to read.
rows.anchor: لم يكن من أهل القراءة والكتابة فلو نزل عليه ذلك جملة واحدة كان لا يضبطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gradual revelation prevents dependence on a written copy and lax memorization, making Muhammad’s retention more complete and his effort greater.
rows.anchor: فالله تعالى ما أعطاه الكتاب دفعة واحدة بل كان ينزل عليه وظيفة ليكون حفظه له أكمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had all scripture descended at once, all laws would have burdened people simultaneously; gradual legislation made compliance easier.
rows.anchor: لو أنزل الكتاب جملة واحدة على الخلق لنزلت الشرائع بأسرها دفعة واحدة على الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing Gabriel repeatedly strengthened Muhammad to convey revelation, bear prophetic trials and harm from his people, and wage jihad.
rows.anchor: إذا شاهد جبريل حالا بعد حال يقوى قلبه بمشاهدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its piecemeal descent still establishes its miraculousness: if humans could produce its like, they could match it in piecemeal form.
rows.anchor: لما تم شرط الإعجاز فيه مع كونه منجما ثبت كونه معجزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation responded to questions and events, increasing insight by joining eloquence with reports of the unseen.
rows.anchor: كان القرآن ينزل بحسب أسئلتهم والوقائع الواقعة لهم فكانوا يزدادون بصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Muhammad challenged them from the start with each newly revealed portion, their inability to match any portion established their inability to match the whole.
rows.anchor: كان يتحداهم من أول الأمر فكأنه تحداهم بكل واحد من نجوم القرآن فلما عجزوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gradual revelation preserved Gabriel’s exalted role as envoy between God and the prophets, carrying God’s message to people.
rows.anchor: السفارة بين الله تعالى وبين أنبيائه وتبليغ كلامه إلى الخلق منصب عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading makes “thus” complete the polytheists’ statement: they wanted a single revelation like the Torah and Gospel, with no omitted words.
rows.anchor: أنه من تمام كلام المشركين أي جملة واحدة كذلك أي كالتوراة والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “thus” begins God’s answer: He sent the Qur’an down in portions to strengthen Muhammad’s heart.
rows.anchor: أنه كلام الله تعالى ذكره جوابا لهم أي كذلك أنزلناه مفرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a demonstrative normally points to something preceding, the objection’s demand for one-time revelation implies a complaint about piecemeal descent, which is what “thus” refers to.
rows.anchor: معناه لم نزل مفرقا فذلك إشارة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartīl in speech means that its parts follow deliberately and at an unhurried pace; the word originally describes gaps between teeth, opposite tightly aligned teeth.
rows.anchor: معنى الترتيل في الكلام أن يأتي بعضه على أثر بعض على تؤدة وتمهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their every new objection is answered with truth that defeats it, as in the image of truth striking down falsehood at 21:18.
rows.anchor: من الجنس الذي تقدم ذكره من الشبهات إلا جئناك بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a better explanation because of its superior clarity; “explanation,” disclosure of a statement’s meaning, is used for the meaning itself.
rows.anchor: وبين أن الذي يأتي به أحسن تفسيرا لأجل ما فيه من المزية في البيان والظهور

words: ٱلَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that people will be resurrected in three groups: mounted, on foot, and on their faces.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: ٱلَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ
rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says that the One who made people walk on their feet can make them walk on their faces.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام : ( إن الذي أمشاهم على أرجلهم قادر

words: ٱلَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase most likely describes the obstinate questioners, though other people of Hell will join them.
rows.anchor: الأقرب أنه صفة للقوم الذين أوردوا هذه الأسئلة على سبيل التعنت

words: ٱلَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reading has them inverted in the afterlife, with faces toward the ground and feet upward; it is attributed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: حمله بعضهم على أنهم يمشون في الآخرة مقلوبين ، وجوههم إلى القرار

words: ٱلَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ
rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers another report: they are dragged face-down; this too is attributed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون المراد أنهم يحشرون ويسحبون على وجوههم

words: ٱلَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ
rows.speaker: الصوفية
rows.claim: Sufis interpret the image inwardly: those attached to anything besides God retain that attachment after death, expressed as being raised on their faces to Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال الصوفية : الذين تعلقت قلوبهم بما سوى الله

words: ٱلَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned are worse in place and more astray than the Garden’s people; this comparison warns against their path, as in the discussion at 25:24.
rows.anchor: ثم بين تعالى أنهم شر مكانا من أهل الجنة وأضل سبيلا وطريقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After discussing divine unity, denial of partners, prophethood and objections to it, and the resurrection, al-Rāzī says the sūra now begins its stories, starting with Moses.
rows.anchor: بعد أن تكلم في التوحيد ونفي الأنداد وإثبات النبوة والجواب عن شبهات المنكرين لها وفي أحوال القيامة شرع في ذكر القصص على السنة المعلومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is likened to clothing because it covers and conceals everything.
rows.anchor: شبه الليل من حيث إنه يستر الكل ويغطي باللباس الساتر للبدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep is called subāt because it causes rest; Abū Muslim likewise defines subāt as rest.
rows.anchor: والسبات هو الراحة وجعل النوم سباتا لأنه سبب للراحة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim relates the name Saturday to customary rest on that day and calls a sick person relieved from illness masbūt.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : السبات الراحة ومنه يوم السبت لما جرت به العادة من الاستراحة فيه ، ويقال للعليل إذا استراح من تعب العلة مسبوت

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf takes subāt as death and masbūt as dead because life has been cut off; he compares it with 6:60.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب ( الكشاف ) السبات الموت والمسبوت الميت لأنه مقطوع الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers “death” to “rest” because the following word, nushūr, is its opposite.
rows.anchor: وإنما قلنا إن تفسيره بالموت أولى من تفسيره بالراحة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim explains daytime nushūr as spreading out and activity.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : وجعل النهار نشورا } هو بمعنى الانتشار والحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an calls sleep a taking of souls, linking waking from sleep with rising from death; 39:42 describes this taking.
rows.anchor: كما سمى تعالى نوم الإنسان وفاة ، فقال : { الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها }

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Luqmān told his son that just as one sleeps and is awakened, one dies and is resurrected.
rows.anchor: وعن لقمان أنه قال لابنه : كما تنام فتوقظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation displays the Creator’s power and blessings: night’s concealment serves many religious and worldly needs.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية مع دلالتها على قدرة الخالق فيها إظهار لنعمه على خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī moves to the next kind, God’s sending of winds, and notes that he explained it earlier in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: النوع الثالث : قوله : { وهو الذى أرسل الرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is read with either singular al-rīḥ or plural al-riyāḥ.
rows.anchor: قرىء ( الريح ) و ( الرياح )

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj lists five vocalic or consonantal forms for nushuran, including forms with initial nūn or bāʾ and a form of bushran with tanwīn.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : وفي ( نشرا ) خمسة أوجه

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim reads bushran as the plural of bashīr, “bearers of good news,” as in 30:46; the nūn reading means winds that spread, as in 77:3.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم في قرأ ( بشرا ) أراد جمع بشير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “mercy” means rain, water, or rainfall.
rows.anchor: والرحمة الغيث والماء والمطر
